title: Optical Coherence Tomography in Pyoderma Gangrenosum: A Pilot Study to Develop Criteria for Initial Diagnosis and Treatment Response
summary:
Background
Pyoderma gangraenosum is a rare inflammatory skin condition that causes painful wounds which can enlarge rapidly. Diagnosing this condition is challenging because the wounds can look similar to other types of chronic leg wounds. Currently, a tissue biopsy is often required to confirm the diagnosis. However, in patients with pyoderma gangraenosum, even minor skin injuries such as a biopsy can trigger a worsening of the wounds.
Research question
This study investigates whether a specialized light-based imaging technique, which does not require a tissue sample and provides high-resolution images of skin structure, can help distinguish pyoderma gangraenosum from other chronic wounds. Additionally, the study examines whether this imaging method can be used to monitor wound healing during treatment.
Methods
The examination is performed using a device that uses light to painlessly image the upper layers of the skin without any incision or tissue removal. For each wound, several images are taken at different points along the wound edge as well as on surrounding healthy skin. A single examination takes only a few minutes and is performed where possible during a routine dressing change, in order to minimize the burden on study participants.

interventions.name: Adult patients (≥ 18 years) with active ulceration due to pyoderma gangraenosum, venous leg ulcer, or hypertensive ischemic leg ulcer. All participants undergo non-invasive OCT examination of the ulceration(s) with four measurements per lesion (one at each wound pole) and two reference measurements

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.    At least 18 years of age at the time of consent.
2.    Clinical suspicion or confirmed diagnosis of pyoderma gangrenosum or venous leg ulcer or hypertensive-ischemic ulcer (HYTILU)
3.    Active ulceration at the time of study enrollment
Exclusion criteria:
1.    Severe pain that prevents an OCT examination.
